title: Ask Forensics: Latency Heuristics Mini Dossier
content:
Purpose:
Quick synth of the most actionable customer asks we keep seeing around inference latency and cost tradeoffs. This is a working note for ENG + SRE + Product to triage small experiments and guardrail fixes. NOT exhaustive — this collects the recurring friction threads and proposes minimal probes.

Topline signals observed (compiled from support threads, field interviews, and runbook incidents):
- Customer A (mid-market search SaaS): KV cache misses spike when varying query length; they reported 2.5x token cost during bursts.
- Customer B (platform team): multi-tenant routing causes regional fallbacks which increase p95 by 180ms intermittently.
- Several customers ask for per-request cache-control hints (ttl, encourage-prefix) — current API has no fine-grained knob.

Representative customer quotes (raw snippets):
- "We keep getting spikes when the prefix changes; it's like cache resets and fees us for every token."
- "Is there a way to pin a model variant for latency-sensitive routes only? We can't afford fallback surprises."

Root-cause hypotheses (quick):
1) Adaptive batching interacts poorly with short, high-frequency requests from PLG flows — batching thresholds too aggressive and cause latency tail.
2) KV cache eviction policy is optimized for average throughput not tail latency; large concurrent sessions evict hot prefixes.
3) Smart routing fallbacks to cost-optimized variants without preserving equivalent KV compatibility, forcing cold start behavior.

Suggested micro-experiments and owners:
- E1: Add per-route cache-hint header (opt-in) to preserve prefixes for high-value routes. Owner: Solutions Eng (Jared). Success metric: 40% reduction in cache-miss token spend for pilot customer.
- E2: Temporarily lower batching window for identified PLG apps during peak (config flag). Owner: Serving Runtime SRE (Lina). Success metric: reduce p95 latency by >=100ms with <3% throughput cost.
- E3: Canary model-variant routing that preserves KV compatibility (no variant fallback unless compatible flag set). Owner: Product-Hosted API + Eng-Serving Runtime. Success metric: zero-cache-invalidations on canary traffic.

Risk and operational notes:
- Cost: per-route pinned caching raises memory usage; need per-customer quota enforcement.
- Complexity: adding an opt-in header requires SDK/CLI updates and docs.
- Observability: need new metric for "cache-miss-token-cost" and sampling traces for eviction events.

Open questions / To validate quickly:
- What are realistic memory footprints per pinned prefix (ask infra to estimate for median model)?
- Can routing preserve KV shape across quantized model-variants? If not, define compatibility matrix.
- Which customers are willing to pilot per-route cost increase in exchange for latency stability? (CS to confirm)

Next steps (next 2 weeks):
1) CS to recruit 2 pilot customers (one PLG-heavy, one enterprise) — Maya.
2) Solutions Eng to draft API sketch for cache-hint header and compatibility semantics — Jared.
3) SRE to run a sim using recent request traces to estimate memory and p95 impact for pinned caching — Lina.
4) Product to schedule 30-min sync with Serving Runtime to align rollout constraints.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this lightweight — aim for 2-week spikes not big design docs.
- Record all test configs into the linked GitHub PR so we can roll back quickly.
- Cross-check with Optimize team suggestions (quantization tips) to avoid redundant experiments.

Appendix (links and raw snippets):

- Short trace dump examples saved in S3: s3://redwood-inference/latency-traces/may-2026/
- Relevant PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/412

End of note.
